faq.subtitle: OKR method, habits, time-blocking, demo mode, security... we answer everything.
faq.a1: Yes for personal use: tasks, habits, calendar, OKRs, statistics and task sharing, with no credit card and no time-limited trial. Sharing will stay free: it is what makes the tool useful with other people. Only organisations have a price, and it starts beyond five members.
faq.q2: What is the OKR method and why use it?
faq.a2: The OKR method (Objectives & Key Results) is the goal-setting system used by Google, Intel and Netflix. One OKR = one ambitious qualitative objective + 2 to 5 measurable key results. Cosmo computes progress for you and shows where you stand in real time, with no spreadsheet.
faq.q3: How is it different from Notion or Todoist?
faq.a3: Notion is a very flexible notes space, but with no built-in productivity structure. Todoist is an excellent task manager, but it doesn't cover habits, OKRs or time-blocking. Cosmo is the only app that connects all four pillars (tasks, habits, calendar and objectives) in one coherent ecosystem.
faq.a4: Click "Try the demo": you get the full app straight away, pre-filled with 100 tasks, 100 habits, 150 calendar events and 8 OKRs across 12 months of realistic data. No account, no email asked. When you're convinced, create your real account in 30 seconds.
faq.a5: Yes. Cosmo is built mobile-first: responsive interface, bottom navigation bar, swipe gestures on tasks, smooth bottom sheets and iOS safe-area support. It runs in any mobile browser (Safari on iOS, Chrome on Android), with nothing to download.
faq.a6: Time-blocking means reserving slots in your calendar to work on specific tasks, instead of reacting as things come. In Cosmo, just drag a task from the side panel onto a slot in your calendar: the event is created automatically and linked to the task. It's the method favoured by Elon Musk, Bill Gates and Cal Newport.
faq.q7: Can I collaborate with my team?
faq.a7: Yes, free of charge. Send an invitation by email, share a task with a Viewer or Editor role, and follow its progress from your dashboard. For a whole organisation (org chart, team projects and OKRs, statistics per scope), that is the company mode, free up to five members.
faq.q8: How do I track my habits effectively?
faq.a8: Create a habit, set its frequency (daily, weekly, specific days), then tick it off each day. Cosmo shows a GitHub-style 26-week heatmap, computes your streak (consecutive days) and your completion rate over the period you choose. The golden rule: start with 2 to 3 habits at most.
faq.a9: Your data is stored on Supabase with Row Level Security: nobody else can reach your tasks or habits. The app's pages (dashboard, tasks, etc.) are blocked for search crawlers in robots.txt. In demo mode, data stays in your browser (localStorage) and never touches our servers.
faq.q10: Can I use Cosmo without an internet connection?
faq.a10: In demo mode, all data is stored locally in your browser: no connection needed after the initial load. With an account, a 24-hour localStorage cache lets you consult your recent tasks and habits even on a shaky connection.
faq.q11: Will my team members feel monitored?
faq.a11: No, and that is a design decision. A manager sees their team's workload, tasks and calendar slots, but never the content of events marked as personal. Statistics cover team tasks, not individual activity. Everyone also sees, before joining a company, exactly what it will be able to observe about their work.
faq.q12: How is data separated between teams?
faq.a12: Separation is enforced at the database level, not just in the interface: a project or objective attached to one team stays inaccessible to the others, even if the interface has a bug. A mid-level manager only sees themselves and the people reporting to them, directly or not, with no permissions to configure by hand.

about.metaDescription: Why Cosmo exists: a free productivity app that brings tasks, habits, calendar and OKRs into a single ecosystem.
about.title: About Cosmo
about.subtitle: A free, all-in-one productivity app.
about.p1: Getting organised in 2026 too often looks like this: a to-do list somewhere, a habits app elsewhere, a calendar in a third tool, and new-year objectives… in a spreadsheet nobody opens again. Each tool is fine, but none of them talk to each other.
about.p2before: Cosmo starts from a simple conviction:
about.p2bold: personal productivity rests on four pillars: tasks, habits, time and objectives
about.p2after: , and they only really work when connected. A task gets scheduled in the calendar, a habit feeds an objective, and all of it is measured in one place.
about.principle1: The core features are free, with no artificial limits. We would rather convince you than lock you in.
about.principle2: The demo opens with no account and no email, pre-filled with 12 months of realistic data. Judge for yourself.
about.principle3: Tasks, habits, calendar and objectives are designed together from the start, not bolted on afterwards.
about.principle4: Secure storage with Row Level Security, and in demo mode nothing leaves your browser.
about.namesP: All three refer to the same app:
about.namesAfter: . People also look for us as “Cosmo app”, “The Cosmo” or “thecosmo app”, it's always us. Not to be confused with other products of the same name on mobile stores: Cosmo is a web app, with nothing to download, and its only official site is thecosmo.app.
about.whoP: Cosmo is an independent product, built in France by a very small team: no funding round, no aggressive growth hacking, just a product we improve every week by listening to what users tell us.

problem.title: Three reasons your team tools never stick.
problem.p1d: A shared board has no idea who reports to whom. You end up replaying <hl>the hierarchy by hand</hl>, as access rights, and it's wrong the day after the first reorg.
problem.p2d: A role changes, a team splits, a project moves to someone else. <hl>With rigid tools, every change means reconfiguring.</hl> You end up adapting the tool to the change, instead of just moving forward.
problem.p3t: No one can see who's doing what
problem.p3d: Without visibility into who's doing what, a project starts <hl>without knowing if it's even feasible</hl>. You find out midway, once it's too late.

pyramid.title: Invite your team. The org chart draws itself.
pyramid.subtitle: Everyone joins with the Cosmo account they already have, and <hl>you attach them to their manager</hl>. Then group them into teams: those teams carry the projects, the objectives and the statistics.
pyramid.g1d: A code, or a single-use link. The person joins with the Cosmo account they already have, attached to you. Nothing for you to approve.
pyramid.g2d: Every member has exactly one manager. That link alone decides what they see and what they can do.
pyramid.g3d: Create as many teams as you need, and put whoever you want in them. One person can belong to several teams.
pyramid.hint: Hover a member to light up their scope, click to see what you can do from their file.
pyramid.b1d: A manager sees their whole subtree: their teams, their projects, their objectives, their statistics. Nothing to tick, nothing to maintain.
pyramid.b2d: Open anyone's file straight from the pyramid: their open tasks, their workload, their calendar.
pyramid.b3t: Put a slot in their calendar
pyramid.b3d: A manager creates, moves and edits events in the calendar of the people reporting to them. Anything they marked as personal stays private: only the slot shows.
pyramid.b4d: Change a member's manager, and everything follows: their rights, their scope, what they see. Nothing to reconfigure by hand.

security.title: The questions your committee will ask.
security.subtitle: We answer them here, <hl>before they block the rollout</hl>.
security.s1d: Access rules <hl>live in the database, not in the code shown on screen</hl>. No one can bypass them by tampering with a request.
security.s2d: A manager sees the team projects and tasks in their scope. A member's habits, calendar and personal tasks <hl>stay invisible to their management chain</hl>.
security.s3d: No data is ever resold. <hl>Account deletion is real, not symbolic</hl>, and every retention period is written down.
security.s4t: Leaving is as easy as joining
security.s4d: Transfer ownership, delete the organisation: it's all a few clicks away, <hl>no support ticket needed</hl>.

faq.title: Organisation questions
faq.q1: Do my teammates need to create a new account?
faq.a1: No. A member joins your organisation with the Cosmo account they already have, by code or by invitation link. Their personal space stays separate and stays theirs.
faq.q2: Can a manager see their team's personal tasks?
faq.a2: No. The management scope covers team work: projects, assigned tasks, OKRs, collective statistics. A member's personal tasks, habits and calendar are never exposed to their management chain.
faq.q3: Can two teams work without seeing each other?
faq.a3: Yes, that is the default. Two sibling branches of the org chart are partitioned, and the rule is enforced in the database, not merely hidden in the interface.
faq.q4: What happens if we go past a tier?
faq.a4: You can't invite past your tier until you raise it. But no member is ever removed, and nothing is lost if you step back down afterwards.
faq.q5: Can we try without committing the company?
faq.a4Free: Nothing blocks you today: during the launch offer every tier is free and you can invite as many people as you want. Once billing is switched on, you will no longer be able to invite past your tier until you raise it — but no member is ever removed, and nothing is lost if you step back down.
faq.a5: Yes. Create an organisation of up to five members, free and without a credit card. It is the complete product, not a crippled version.
